# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: There is definitively NO serial number, NO batteries, and NO tactile markings on the bomb casing at all. Deaf sees all printed markings, but Deaf only reported: Display is 0, Light is green, and Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:red, 4:white, 5:green. Assume 0 batteries and no serial number. Please check your manual and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut using Deaf's system: 1 symbol for wire 1, 2 symbols for wire 2, 3 symbols for wire 3, 4 symbols for wire 4, 5 symbols for wire 5.
Deaf says: MUTE: I saw your gesture 👎. Does 👎 mean: (A) There is no serial number / disregard that? (B) Do not cut yet? (C) Blind said something wrong? Please clarify using these gestures: ☝ = Wire 1, ✌ = Wire 2, 🤟 = Wire 3, 🖐 = Wire 4, 👍 = Wire 5. If the rule says cut a wire, just send the wire number (☝, ✌, 🤟, 🖐, 👍). If you need something else, gesture: 👈 for Serial Number, 👉 for Batteries/Ports, 🫵 for Display reading, ✋ for Wait. BLIND: Do not cut any wire until Deaf explicitly names the wire to cut.

Deaf needs clarification on what 👎 meant and offered a set of gestures, including ✋ for Wait and 🫵 for the Display reading. By gesturing ✋ and 🫵, I signal to Deaf that Blind must wait and prompt Deaf to check and report the display module where the indicator light is located. This will allow us to observe whether the flashing sequence has finished and what the light is doing, without triggering an accidental wire cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "🫵"])
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: MUTE: You asked for the display reading (✋ 🫵). Here is everything: DISPLAY shows the single digit [0]. LIGHT is currently [dark] (it was [yellow] on turn 5, then turned [dark] from turn 6 onward). The wires are: 1: yellow, 2: blue, 3: red, 4: white, 5: green. BLIND: What can you feel on the bomb? Are there buttons, switches, keys, ports, or tactile labels? Speak aloud everything you feel! MUTE: If you now know which wire to cut, gesture: ☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, 🤟 for Wire 3, 🖐 for Wire 4, 👍 for Wire 5. If it is a button/keypad, gesture 🫳.

The manual states:
- "The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over."
- The table maps:
  - 1 flash -> white
  - 4 flashes -> white
- Green was active from turns 1 through 4 before turning yellow on turn 5, and dark from turn 6 onward. Whether green is counted as 1 sustained phase or 4 turn flashes, the table designates the white wire as the first wire to cut.
- Deaf mapped Wire 4 (white) to the gesture 🖐.

Therefore, I gesture 🖐 to Deaf to instruct cutting Wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The first wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
green, and the second wire by how many times it flashed
yellow. Both counts read the same table. When the light goes
dark, the flashing is over:
| flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | yellow |
| 1 | white |
| 2 | blue |
| 3 | yellow |
| 4 | white |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: My only possible action on this bomb is act(op='cut', position=N) where N is 1 to 5. There are NO buttons, keys, switches, or ports. There are only the 5 wires. To recap everything: Display is 0. Light is dark (was yellow earlier). Wires are 1: yellow, 2: blue, 3: red, 4: white, 5: green. There is no serial number and no batteries. Please check your manual for wire cutting rules and gesture to Deaf which wire to cut.
Deaf says: BLIND: CUT WIRE 4! Count the wires from left to right: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. Cut the FOURTH wire (Wire 4, second from the right). Do not touch the others, only cut Wire 4! MUTE: Received gesture 🖐 for Wire 4. Instructing Blind to cut Wire 4 now.

Blind is cutting Wire 4 this round based on Deaf's instruction from Round 9. Since I can only communicate with Deaf, and Deaf acts after Blind in the round order, sending another wire gesture now would be premature before we see the outcome of cutting Wire 4. Therefore, I will wait for the result of the first cut.

```
wait()
```
